key_insight: Different flow paths can produce the same flow-matching objective but very different gradient variance, so path choice can materially speed up or slow down SGD.
engineering_relevance: For practical diffusion/flow-matching training, optimizing the interpolation/path construction can reduce training cost without changing the target distribution or model objective.
method: Analyze SGD variance for flow matching under a family of paths that preserve the same marginals and velocity field.
Derive a tight iteration-complexity bound for a linear velocity model with 1D Gaussian data and identify an optimal linear path.
Formulate a constrained path-selection problem (PathOpt_θ) and convert it into sample-estimable constraints for numerical search.
evidence_signal: The paper reports theoretical variance/complexity analysis and validates it experimentally on Gaussian data, Gaussian mixture models, and real datasets.
watch_item: Variance reduction alone is not sufficient; the path must stay in the equivalence class G(p_t, v*_t), which is generally hard to verify exactly.
paper_title: Same Flow, Different Paths: Variance Reduction in Flow Matching
